messages.author: 7f3170e7815a360a
messages.subject: error with geom_rect()
parts:
Hi all,

I am trying to do something basic, but I get an error that I don't
know how to fix. I am trying to add a background color to a plot. The
code for the plot is working fine. Yet, if I add the line after
geom_rect() it doesn't produce any background color and, in addition,
it generates an error ( the plots is still produced, though).

> head(c)
DEM DIC total prop.dem year date
1967 39 99 138 0.28 1967 1967-01-01
1968 38 104 142 0.27 1968 1968-01-01
1969 37 105 142 0.26 1969 1969-01-01
1970 37 108 145 0.26 1970 1970-01-01
1971 38 110 148 0.26 1971 1971-01-01
1972 37 112 149 0.25 1972 1972-01-01
> qplot(date,abs(prop.dem),data=c,size=total,geom=c("point"),
+ main="Democracy Over Time Across the World") +
opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=00,hjust=.5),size=5)
> + geom_rect(aes(xmin = 1979, xmax = 1992, ymin = .1, ymax =.6))
Error in +geom_rect(aes(xmin = 1979, xmax = 1992, ymin = 0.1, ymax =
0.6)) :
invalid argument to unary operator
>

Any suggestions? Thanks!

Antonio.

messages.author: 7c598f9d5aed052f
messages.subject: Re: error with geom_rect()
parts: Put the last two lines into one, i.e.

The resulting graph is probably not what you want, but you avoid the error.

Reason for the error is that your command is terminated in the line
> opts(axis.text.x=theme_text(angle=00,hjust=.5),size=5)
and you start a new command (rather than continuing the prior one) with
> + ....
which ( I believe) is the rejected "unary operator".

In my (admittedly very limited) experience, it is better to use ggplot
rather than qplot if you want to do more sophisticated stuff.

Rgds,
Rainer

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: error with geom_rect()
parts:
Here's a reproducible example:

ggplot(df, aes(x = year, y = y)) +
geom_rect(aes(NULL, NULL, xmin = 1990, xmax = 2000,
ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
fill = alpha(c('orange'), 0.2) ) +
geom_line(size = 1)

Does that help?

Dennis

messages.author: 4fdc04b06b76c8cf
messages.subject: Mix log and continous scale in facet wrap?
parts:
Hello,

I do have several plots and they all share the same y-axis.
Thats why I wanted to combine them using facet wrap.

But my single plots do have different extent in the x axis and I want
for some of them that the x axis is log scaled and for others just
continous scaled. I set the axis with scales = "free_x".

Is there any possibilty to define different scales for my single
x-axis?

I read something about subset but I am not sure if that is also
the solution for that? I couldn't find any parameter in scale_continuous
so that the scale only applies to some but not all plots.

Thank you very much

Johannes

after a day trying around with different x-axis for the single
plots in facet_wrap I think I'll give up.

I will now just make the single plots with ggplot2 and arrange them
with grid.arrange. Thus some question appeared:

1) Is it possible to remove the ticks of a plot only on one axis? If yes how? I know that I can do it with "axis.ticks = theme_blank()" for both axis.

2) Is it somehow possible to replace the bottom axis title with a title
in a grey box above the plot, so that it looks like in facet_wrap. Because
I think that looks much cleaner when arraning multiple plots on one page.

3)I'd like to arrange the single plots in two columns (with grid.arrange). How can I set the margin between the two columns? Or how can I make that the plots are closer togehter (like in facet_wrap)?
